abstract: Distinct stem cell clones can yield similar lineage outputs via different developmental trajectories or dynamics and respond differently to perturbation. Here, we introduce ChronoClone, an unsupervised method that groups single-cell clones by time-resolved cell-state composition into metaclones. Benchmarked against simulated ground-truth scenarios, ChronoClone demonstrates high noise tolerance compared to existing methods. Applied to an adult mouse hematopoietic lineage-tracing dataset, ChronoClone showed that clones producing the same lineage mature at different speeds, a difference the original study did not examine. Furthermore, using WT metaclones as a baseline reference for Dnmt3a- and Npm1c-mutant sister-clones, ChronoClone uncovered hidden, clone-specific mutation responses including slowed maturation and lineage composition shifts. By connecting temporal dynamics, perturbation responses, and ancestral molecular states, ChronoClone adds temporal cell-state dynamics into clonal analysis.
